clue.text: Male in charge gets on to Exmoor resident about place names

indicators.note: the male takes the moorland animal right into his own letters, so one word sits inside the other here

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so male gives TOM
the Exmoor is a breed of pony native to that English moorland

explanation.surface: A man in charge mounts a moorland pony while thinking about place names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets on to' signals the animal going inside the male. Exmoor is a moorland area of south-west England known for its wild ponies.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective relating to toponyms is one concerned with the names of places, so it fits the phrase.

clue.text: An extinct bird on Society island group

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for Society, as in RSPCA-style initials
an gives the letter A
the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct

explanation.surface: A vanished bird is found on a Pacific island in the Society group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Society Islands are a real Pacific group, which makes 'Society island' read as one name; in fact Society is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is a chain of Polynesian islands in the South Pacific, an archipelago or island group.

clue.text: Mythical beast mangled closest men with horns

indicators.note: something mangled is crushed and twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legendary creature has savaged the nearest men with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The creature said to live in a Scottish loch is a legendary monster whose existence is unproven.

clue.text: English left with yen for fairness

parts.note: quit means departed, as left does
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: An Englishman departs with a longing for a fair deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' poses as a longing, but it is the currency abbreviation Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is impartial justice, a synonym for fairness and even-handedness.

clue.text: Cassette missing — and record: silence!

parts.note: with the cassette absent there is no tape
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A frustrated person finds the tape gone and demands quiet so they can play a record.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an instruction meaning not the slightest sound, an order for complete quiet.

clue.text: A new short bone in the ear inhibiting growth

indicators.note: the bone named is cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the tibia is the shinbone
otic is the medical adjective meaning relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A recently found tiny bone in the ear is said to stunt growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TIBIA to TIBI. The ear's tiny bones (ossicles) make the surface plausible, but the bone is the shin's.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibiotic drugs work by stopping bacteria from multiplying, so as an adjective it describes something that inhibits growth.

clue.text: Defeat with thin metal sword

definitions.meaning: to thwart or defeat a plan
... is metal beaten into a very thin sheet, as in kitchen ...

explanation.surface: Someone is beaten by a slim metal blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has three senses: to thwart, a thin sheet of metal, and a light fencing weapon.

clue.text: Steers round most of adjacent turning

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: turning means the trimmed word is read backwards
most of the word means all but its final letter

parts.note: next means adjacent or neighbouring

explanation.surface: A driver steers around a nearby bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of the synonym, leaving NEX, and 'turning' reads that backwards. 'Steers' looks like a verb but is the plural noun for young bullocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Steers are castrated male cattle, and oxen are cattle used as draught animals, so the words match.

clue.text: Disloyal to America without justification

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the outer pieces enclose the middle one

parts.note: taken as written
a reason is a justification for something
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of betraying America for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The surface reading of 'without justification' is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasonous acts betray one's country, so the adjective means disloyal in the gravest way.

clue.text: Leaving out old floor covering where I replaced area

indicators.note: the letter I takes the place of the letter for area in the covering word

parts.note: matting is a coarse covering laid on floors
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone skips an old rug in a room where they have changed the space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' signals the swap of one letter for another; 'where' is just a link. 'Leaving out' must be read as a verb form, matching the -ing answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitting something means not including it, the same as leaving it out.

clue.text: What holds back stock song included by La Traviata's leads

indicators.note: the song sits inside the two opening letters
the leads of the words are their first letters

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: An opera fan recalls a stirring song from Verdi's La Traviata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' takes L and T from 'La Traviata's', and 'included by' puts ARIA between them. La Traviata is a Verdi opera, so the song looks part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso used by cowboys to catch and restrain cattle, which is livestock or stock.

clue.text: Imply 13 across could be creating disharmony

indicators.note: says the letters could be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the answer at 13 across, a drug that stops bacterial growth

explanation.surface: Suggesting a drug might cause a bad reaction with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IMPLY and the 13 across answer are mixed together; 'creating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Incompatibility is a failure to get along or fit together, which is a state of disharmony.

clue.text: Son's in gallery for brief experience

indicators.note: the son's letter goes inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a group of art galleries in London and elsewhere in Britain
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A son is at an art gallery for a short visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous British art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste is a small sample or short first experience of something, as in a taste of fame.

clue.text: Coming to avoid wingers in ball control

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes inside the other

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: the wingers are the outside letters, which are left off

explanation.surface: A footballer coming in, avoiding the wingers, keeps control of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid wingers' strips the outer letters, and 'in' places what is left inside the dance word. The football picture makes 'ball' look like the round thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is the exercise of power or supremacy over others, which is control.

clue.text: Wavelike mark left in flood

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the water word

parts.note: a flood or rising flow of water is a tide

explanation.surface: A wave-shaped stain is left after a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy accent mark used over letters such as the Spanish n.

clue.text: Aid recovery of the constituent run over by trucks

indicators.note: the trucks go over and around the other words, enclosing them

parts.note: pickups are light trucks with an open back
taken as written
a piece is a part or constituent of a whole

explanation.surface: A voter is hit by lorries and needs help to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run over by' signals the trucks enclosing the other pieces. The grim surface of a voter knocked down hides a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to restore order after a disaster, helping things recover.

clue.text: Carbon molecule now mostly found in liquid butane

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the rearranged letters
liquid suggests the letters flow into a new shape
most of the word, without its final letter

explanation.surface: A carbon molecule is now usually found in liquefied butane gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter; 'liquid' rearranges the gas, giving NATUBE; 'found in' places the short word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanotube is a tiny cylinder of carbon atoms, a molecular structure studied in materials science.

clue.text: Birds with head down are deep in thought

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is moved down to the bottom in this down clue

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Birds with their heads lowered seem to be thinking hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head down' moves the E of EMUS to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or meditate, so it means being lost in thought.

clue.text: Daisy's family make music: one cheers being entertained

indicators.note: the two short pieces are entertained, held inside the music word

parts.note: to compose is to write music
I is the Roman numeral one
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A family named Daisy makes music while one guest gets drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being entertained' puts ITA inside COMPOSE. Ta and cheers are both informal British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Compositae is the botanical name of the large plant family that includes daisies, asters and sunflowers.

clue.text: Ancient mariner in story of fall from grace with evil

parts.note: sin is a moral lapse, a fall from grace
bad means evil or wicked

explanation.surface: An old sailor's tale tells of disgrace and wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient mariner' recalls Coleridge's poem, but the sailor is from the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad the Sailor is a legendary seafarer in the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Pair often upset with motion, something two may not agree on

definitions.text: something two may not agree on

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A couple often argue over a proposal on which they disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: A question that is a matter of opinion is open to debate, so two people can disagree about it.

clue.text: Organised car pool is a strong point for city

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-run car-sharing scheme is a city's great asset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong point' looks like an asset; it is a fortified height.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified citadel on high ground in an ancient Greek city, a stronghold.

clue.text: Carriage being prepared to go to square

indicators.note: the second piece goes onto the first, joining it in order

parts.note: four is a square number, two times two
work in hand is being dealt with or prepared

explanation.surface: A coach is made ready to set off for the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: IN HAND goes after FOUR. 'square' looks like a place but is the square number.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-in-hand is a carriage drawn by four horses driven by one person.

clue.text: A ball game with most important part for defender

parts.note: polo is a ball game played on horseback
the gist is the essential point of something

explanation.surface: In a ball game the key position is that of a defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defender' sounds like a sports position, but it is one who speaks up for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in defence of a belief or cause, so is its defender.

clue.text: Gift people brought to party

indicators.note: the second word is brought to the first and set after it

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Guests bring a present to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is something given freely, a gift to a cause.

clue.text: Hold back fashion when replacing large with medium one

indicators.note: the medium and one letters take the place of the letter for large

parts.note: style means fashion
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing labels
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fashion is curbed when medium sizes replace large ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps L in STYLE for MI. Clothing sizes make the surface coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart, preventing progress, which is holding something back.

clue.text: What gets used in homeopathy medicines

definitions.text: What gets used in homeopathy medicines

indicators.note: the herb sits within the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A herb is used in alternative remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb sits across 'homeopathy medicines', and the herb is itself used in such remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used in herbal and homeopathic remedies as well as cooking.

clue.text: Company — one providing cones on motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a fir is a conifer, a tree that bears cones
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A firm supplies traffic cones for the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Traffic cones on a motorway suggest roadworks, but the cones are those of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a business, the same as a company.
